Meslek ve bölüm eşleştirmesi, yalnızca i: Matching occupations to majors is done not just by comparing the names, but by the semantic (context/meaning) similarity of the full description text of both. The reason: when only the name is used, words that have no real semantic relationship but look alike at the letter/syllable level (e.g. two words that come from a common root but have entirely different meanings) can confuse the model. When the full description is used, the model focuses on what the word actually means rather than its superficial appearance — and this largely eliminates the wrong matches caused by name similarity.

Therefore, for each layer, we compute the probability that at least 2 of the 3 models would pick the same candidate if they guessed completely at random: C(3,2)·p²(1−p) + p³, p = 1/number of candidates (e.g. 7 candidates in K1, 9 in K4).
